sentences.zh: 这里是《每日新闻》。

sentences.en: Today, she was the most famous Black woman in America who exposed the systematic lynching of Black men.
sentences.zh: 今天的主角是美国最著名的黑人女性，她揭露了针对黑人男性的系统性私刑。

sentences.en: But when she died, the Times failed to write an obituary.
sentences.zh: 但当她逝世时，《纽约时报》却没有为她写讣告。

sentences.en: How the paper of record is trying to fix the record.
sentences.zh: 这家权威大报正试图修正历史记录。

sentences.en: Friday, March 16th.
sentences.zh: 3月16日，星期五。

sentences.en: And, uh, so how did the two of them meet, do you know?
sentences.zh: 那么，呃，你知道他们俩是怎么认识的吗？

sentences.en: Obits are about life.
sentences.zh: 讣告是关于一生的。

sentences.en: I think that's why people love them so much.
sentences.zh: 我想这也是为什么人们如此喜爱它们。

sentences.en: They're relatable, they're interesting, they're little nuggets of history.
sentences.zh: 它们贴近生活，引人入胜，是一块块历史的碎片。

sentences.en: At a concert with James Brown?
sentences.zh: 在詹姆斯·布朗的演唱会上吗？

sentences.en: Often about things you never knew.
sentences.zh: 通常讲述你从未了解过的事情。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: And the cause of death was cancer?
sentences.zh: 死因是癌症吗？

sentences.en: Do we know what kind?
sentences.zh: 你知道是什么类型的癌症吗？

sentences.en: It's almost as though you have to be part therapist when you talk to families.
sentences.zh: 与家属交谈时，你几乎觉得自己得兼任心理治疗师。

sentences.en: Oh, boy.
sentences.zh: 天哪。

sentences.en: Repeating back what you're hearing.
sentences.zh: 重复你所听到的内容。

sentences.en: Was this sudden or, uh, was he ailing for a while?
sentences.zh: 这是突然发生的，还是说，呃，他病了一段时间了？

sentences.en: Kind of almost consoling them in some cases when they get very emotional.
sentences.zh: 在某些情况下，当他们情绪非常激动时，你几乎是在安慰他们。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: My dad died of the same thing.
sentences.zh: 我父亲也是因同样的病去世的。

sentences.en: I know that's tough.
sentences.zh: 我知道这很难受。

sentences.en: You're trying so hard to understand every detail about this person without ever having met them.
sentences.zh: 你明明从未见过这个人，却在拼命了解关于他的一切细节。

sentences.en: Mm-hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯哼。

sentences.en: Yeah, that's way too young, too.
sentences.zh: 是啊，这也实在太年轻了。

sentences.en: And it's a difficult thing to do when you're talking to somebody who's grieving.
sentences.zh: 当你在和悲痛欲绝的人交谈时，这真是一件很难做到的事。

sentences.en: So I feel like you have to want a job like this.
sentences.zh: 所以我觉得你必须打心底里想做这样一份工作。

sentences.en: Thank you.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: And again, my condolences.
sentences.zh: 再次向您致以哀悼。

sentences.en: Bye-bye.
sentences.zh: 再见。

sentences.en: I think who gets remembered and how inherently involves judgment.
sentences.zh: 我认为，谁能被铭记以及如何被铭记，本质上涉及一种判断。

sentences.en: It's news judgment, but it's still some form of judgment.
sentences.zh: 这是新闻判断，但它依然是一种形式的判断。

sentences.en: And to look back at the obituary archives can paint a picture of what society valued and who.
sentences.zh: 回顾讣告档案，可以勾勒出社会曾珍视什么以及珍视谁的图景。

sentences.en: Amy Podnani works on the obits desk at the Times, where every morning dozens of submissions pour into her inbox.
sentences.zh: 艾米·波德纳尼在《纽约时报》讣告组工作，每天清晨，数以十计的投稿如潮水般涌入她的收件箱。

sentences.en: Candidates for a New York Times obituary.
sentences.zh: 这些都是《纽约时报》讣告的候选人。

sentences.en: All right.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: So here we have our liSt. At the top, we have the people we know we're definitely going to do.
sentences.zh: 所以，这是我们的名单。排在最前面的，是我们确定一定会写的人。

sentences.en: We're just waiting to assign them when we have a reporter free.
sentences.zh: 我们只是在等待一有空闲的记者就分配任务。

sentences.en: And then underneath that, we have a list called to be vetted.
sentences.zh: 在那下面，我们有一个名为“待审核”的名单。

sentences.en: And in this case, this morning, we heard about Ethel Stein, who was credited with getting the patent for sock puppets.
sentences.zh: 在这个清晨，我们听说了埃塞尔·斯坦的事迹，她因获得袜子木偶的专利而闻名。

sentences.en: So we decided to assign that one right away.
sentences.zh: 所以我们决定立刻把这个任务派出去。

sentences.en: But we'll ask each other questions.
sentences.zh: 但我们会互相提问。

sentences.en: We'll pick each other's brains about, well, did they really do this?
sentences.zh: 我们会集思广益，讨论：他们真的做过这件事吗？

sentences.en: Well, were they the first to do that?
sentences.zh: 嗯，他们是第一个这么做的吗？

sentences.en: Well, is there a good story to tell?
sentences.zh: 嗯，这是一个值得讲述的好故事吗？

sentences.en: I think approximately 150,000 people die between one edition of the newspaper and the next.
sentences.zh: 我想在报纸的两个版次之间，大约有15万左右的人去世。

sentences.en: Of course, we don't hear about all of those.
sentences.zh: 当然，我们不会得知所有这些人的消息。

sentences.en: We hear about a sliver.
sentences.zh: 我们听说的只是九牛一毛。

sentences.en: And then of those, we have to pick three.
sentences.zh: 而在这些人中，我们必须挑选出三个。

sentences.en: So it's a difficult job for sure.
sentences.zh: 所以这绝对是一项艰难的工作。

sentences.en: Shortly after she joined the team, she started getting emails from readers who were noticing the people left out.
sentences.zh: 加入团队不久后，她开始收到读者的电子邮件，他们注意到被遗漏的人。

sentences.en: Why don't you have more women and people of color in your pages?
sentences.zh: 为什么你们版面上没有更多的女性和有色人种？

sentences.en: You focus too much on white men.
sentences.zh: 你们太关注白人男性了。

sentences.en: And as a woman of color, this resonated with me.
sentences.zh: 作为一个有色人种女性，这引起了我的共鸣。

sentences.en: And I wondered about it too.
sentences.zh: 我也对此感到好奇。

sentences.en: And I kind of tucked it in the corner of my mind.
sentences.zh: 我把它默默记在了心底的某个角落。

sentences.en: And then one day, Amy discovered that the woman who brought tennis to the United States never got an obituary.
sentences.zh: 直到有一天，艾米发现将网球运动带到美国的女性居然从未获得过讣告。

sentences.en: So then I tucked that away in the corner of my mind.
sentences.zh: 于是我把这件事也收在了心底的角落。

sentences.en: And it sent her on a journey to see who else the New York Times missed.
sentences.zh: 这开启了她的一段旅程，去寻找《纽约时报》还遗漏了谁。

sentences.en: We often say that obituaries are kind of a rearview look at society.
sentences.zh: 我们经常说，讣告是对社会的一种后视镜式的回顾。

sentences.en: They aren't representing society as we see it today.
sentences.zh: 它们并不代表我们今天所看到的社会。

sentences.en: They're representing a couple of generations ago.
sentences.zh: 它们代表的是几个世代之前的社会。

sentences.en: And a couple of generations ago, women and people of color were not really invited to the table to make a difference the way white men were.
sentences.zh: 而在几个世代前，女性和有色人种并没有真正被邀请上谈判桌，无法像白人男性那样发挥影响力。

sentences.en: So we thought maybe this was the perfect time to tell their stories.
sentences.zh: 所以我们认为，这或许是讲述他们故事的绝佳时机。

sentences.en: The list was long.
sentences.zh: 名单很长。

sentences.en: There were a lot of big names that surprised us.
sentences.zh: 有很多让我们感到意外的大人物。

sentences.en: There was Diane Arbus, the brilliant photographer.
sentences.zh: 有才华横溢的摄影师黛安·阿勃丝。

sentences.en: Sylvia Plath, the poet.
sentences.zh: 诗人西尔维娅·普拉斯。

sentences.en: There was Charlotte Bronte, the writer who wrote Jane Eyre.
sentences.zh: 还有写作《简·爱》的作家夏洛蒂·勃朗特。

sentences.en: Another one was Ida B.
sentences.zh: 还有一个是伊达·B·

sentences.en: Wells.
sentences.zh: 韦尔斯。

sentences.en: She was a journalist and suffragist who pioneered the anti-lynching campaign.
sentences.zh: 她是一位记者兼女性选举权运动者，开创了反私刑运动先河。

sentences.en: She was one of the first people to create a newspaper by a Black person for Black people specifically.
sentences.zh: 她是第一批创办专门由黑人为了黑人发声的报纸的人之一。

sentences.en: And she was considered one of the most successful Black people alive at the time.
sentences.zh: 在当时，她被认为是世上最成功的黑人之一。

sentences.en: And oddly, we had a little notice on the front page of the New York Times when she got married, but we had absolutely nothing about her death.
sentences.zh: 奇怪的是，当她结婚时，《纽约时报》头版曾有一则小通知，但对于她的死，我们却字全无。

sentences.en: When the editors came to me with this project, I can't say that I was surprised to learn that the New York Times didn't write about Ida B.
sentences.zh: 当编辑们带着这个项目找到我时，我不能说得知《纽约时报》没有报道伊达·B·

sentences.en: Wells' death, but it was very, very striking.
sentences.zh: 韦尔斯的死让我感到惊讶，但这非常、非常醒目。

sentences.en: Caitlin Dickerson is a national reporter for The Times.
sentences.zh: 凯特琳·迪克森是《时报》的国家新闻记者。

sentences.en: Ida B.
sentences.zh: 伊达·B·

sentences.en: Wells was born a slave in 1862 in Holly Springs, Mississippi.
sentences.zh: 韦尔斯于1862年出生在密西西比州霍利斯普林斯的奴隶家庭。

sentences.en: This is the heart of the
sentences.zh: 这里是

sentences.en: Deep South.
sentences.zh: 美国深南部的腹地。

sentences.en: And the next year, slaves are emancipated.
sentences.zh: 第二年，奴隶获得了解放。

sentences.en: So she grows up during this period of Reconstruction where you see dramatic Black advancement.
sentences.zh: 因此，她在重建时期长大，见证了黑人权益的戏剧性飞跃。

sentences.en: Black people go from being slaves to being able to vote, including Ida B.
sentences.zh: 黑人从奴隶变成了拥有投票权的人，其中包括伊达·B·

sentences.en: Wells' father.
sentences.zh: 韦尔斯的父亲。

sentences.en: You even see some being elected into state legislatures.
sentences.zh: 你甚至能看到一些人当选为州议员。

sentences.en: My earliest recollections are of reading the newspaper to my father and an admiring group of his friends.
sentences.zh: 我最早的记忆就是给父亲和他一群崇拜他的朋友读报纸。

sentences.en: He was interested in politics, and I heard the words Ku Klux Klan long before I knew what they meant.
sentences.zh: 他对政治很感兴趣，早在明白其含义之前，我就听过“三K党”这个词。

sentences.en: I knew dimly that it meant something fearful by the anxious way my mother walked to the floor at night when my father was out to a political meeting.
sentences.zh: 从母亲在父亲外出参加政治会议的夜晚在地板上焦虑踱步的样子，我隐约知道这意味着某种可怕的事情。

sentences.en: Our job was to go to school and learn all we could.
sentences.zh: 我们的工作就是去学校尽可能多地学习知识。

sentences.en: And then when Ida B.
sentences.zh: 然后在伊达·B·

sentences.en: Wells is 16 years old, her parents and a sibling, she's one of eight, they die of yellow fever.
sentences.zh: 韦尔斯16岁时，她的父母和一个兄弟姐妹（她是八个孩子中的一个）死于黄热病。

sentences.en: So she takes on caring for the rest of her siblings.
sentences.zh: 于是她承担起了照顾其余兄弟姐妹的重任。

sentences.en: She starts to work as a teacher after she drops out of high school, and she finishes her own education at night and on the weekends.
sentences.zh: 她在高中辍学后开始当老师，并在夜间和周末完成自己的学业。

sentences.en: And I think this experience, as hard as it was, it's really emboldening for her more than anything else, right?
sentences.zh: 我认为这段经历尽管艰难，但对她来说比什么都更能赋予她勇气，对吧？

sentences.en: She's 16 years old, a black girl in the South, but it gives her the sense that she can do a lot more than I think another woman in her circumstances might have even been able to
sentences.zh: 她才16岁，是南方的黑人女孩，但它让她觉得，她能做的事远比我想象中处境相似的其他女性所能

sentences.en: fathom.
sentences.zh: 想象的要多得多。

sentences.en: And she applies that boldness almost right away because there's a dramatic whiplash in the
sentences.zh: 她几乎立刻就展现了这种大胆，因为

sentences.en: South.
sentences.zh: 南方经历了戏剧性的急转直下。

sentences.en: Almost all of these advancements that come out of Reconstruction are reversed in the form of Jim
sentences.zh: 重建时期带来的几乎所有进步，都以吉姆·克劳法的形式被

sentences.en: Crow.
sentences.zh: 逆转了。

sentences.en: This is where you see racial segregation codified into law.
sentences.zh: 在这里，你看到种族隔离被写进了法律。

sentences.en: And with Jim Crow comes a kind of cultural acceptance of violence against African Americans.
sentences.zh: 伴随着吉姆·克劳法而来的，是一种对针对非裔美国人暴力的文化默许。

sentences.en: And the worst example of this is lynching.
sentences.zh: 而这其中最糟糕的例子就是私刑。

sentences.en: So there's a period from the 1890s to the early 1900s when lynchings number in the thousands, and you see crowds of people gather to watch these murders take place in cold blood.
sentences.zh: 因此，从19世纪90年代到20世纪初，有一个时期的私刑数量达数千起之多，你会看到成群的人聚集在一起，冷血地观看这些谋杀发生。

sentences.en: Arriving here at 12 o'clock, the train was met by a surging mass of humanity, 10,000 strong.
sentences.zh: 火车于12点抵达这里时，迎面而来的是汹涌的人潮，足足有一万人之多。

sentences.en: They cheer and celebrate almost as if they're watching a sporting event.
sentences.zh: 他们欢呼庆祝，简直就像在观看体育赛事。

sentences.en: The Negro was placed upon a carnival float in mockery of a king upon his throne.
sentences.zh: 那个黑人被放在狂欢的花车上，以此嘲弄宝座上的国王。

sentences.en: So Ida is a journalist at the time.
sentences.zh: 当时伊达是一名记者。

sentences.en: She's moved from Mississippi to Memphis, and she's watching and covering and watching and covering these lynchings.
sentences.zh: 她从密西西比搬到了孟菲斯，一直在观察、报道、再观察和报道这些私刑。

sentences.en: Here, Smith was placed upon a scaffold, six feet square and 10 feet high, securely bound within the view of all the beholders.
sentences.zh: 在这里，史密斯被绑在一个六英尺见方、十英尺高的脚手架上，在所有目击者的注视下被牢牢捆绑。

sentences.en: Here, the victim was tortured for 50 minutes by red hot iron brands thrust against his quivering body.
sentences.zh: 在这里，受害者被通红的铁烙铁炙烤着颤抖的身体，折磨了50分钟。

sentences.en: Commencing at the feet, the brands were placed upon him inch by inch until they were thrust against the face.
sentences.zh: 从双脚开始，烙铁一寸一寸地按在他身上，直到被烫到脸上。

sentences.en: He pleaded and writhed in bodily and mental pain.
sentences.zh: 他在肉体和精神的痛苦中哀求、翻滚。

sentences.en: Then kerosene was poured upon him.
sentences.zh: 然后有人将煤油倒在他身上。

sentences.en: Cotton seed holes placed beneath him and set on fire.
sentences.zh: 把棉籽壳垫在他身下并点燃。

sentences.en: She's observing these lynchings take place, and she views them as what she calls a violent form of
sentences.zh: 她目睹了这些私刑的发生，并将其视为她所称的“一种暴力的

sentences.en: subjugation, to terrorize Black people so much that they become scared into submission.
sentences.zh: 征服形式”，用以恐吓黑人，让他们恐惧到顺从。

sentences.en: His clothes were torn off piecemeal and scattered in the crowd, people catching the shreds and putting them away as mementos.
sentences.zh: 他的衣服被一块块撕碎并散落在人群中，人们抓住这些碎片留作纪念品。

sentences.en: And even when it's over, people mutilate the body as they take fingernails and pieces of rope as souvenirs.
sentences.zh: 即便在结束后，人们仍把指甲和绳索剪下来作为纪念品，残害尸体。

sentences.en: It was horrible.
sentences.zh: 这太可怕了。

sentences.en: Every groan from the fiend, every contortion of his body was cheered by the thickly packed crowd of 10,000 persons.
sentences.zh: 那个恶魔的每一次呻吟、身体的每一次扭曲，都赢得了密密麻麻挤满的一万名观众的欢呼。

sentences.en: Hundreds of people turned away, but the vast crowd still looked calmly on.
sentences.zh: 数百人转身离去，但庞大的人群依然平静地冷眼旁观。

sentences.en: Caitlin, this sounds like an especially kind of awful beat to have covering lynchings.
sentences.zh: 凯特琳，报道私刑听起来真是一份特别糟糕的跑口工作。

sentences.en: You have here an
sentences.zh: 你这里有一位

sentences.en: African-American journalist and editor who seems to have made it the focus of her journalism.
sentences.zh: 非裔美国记者兼编辑，她似乎将此作为自己新闻报道的核心。

sentences.en: How did she handle that?
sentences.zh: 她是怎么处理这件事的？

sentences.en: How does she react to it?
sentences.zh: 她对此有何反应？

sentences.en: I think it's hard to overstate how difficult this coverage must have been for her as a journaliSt. And in fact, there's one lynching in particular that really
sentences.zh: 我认为无论怎么强调对她作为一名记者来说这种报道有多么困难都不为过。事实上，有一场私刑尤其彻底

sentences.en: changes everything for her.
sentences.zh: 改变了她的一切。

sentences.en: And that's when a close friend of hers named Thomas Moss is himself lynched.
sentences.zh: 那就是她的挚友托马斯·莫斯本人遭到私刑杀害。

sentences.en: He was part owner of a grocery store and he ends up being killed over a fight that breaks out between black and white children who are playing marbles.
sentences.zh: 他是杂货店的合伙人，最终因为黑白儿童玩弹珠引发的一场争吵而被杀害。

sentences.en: He's arrested over this fight, brought into jail, and then in the middle of the night, a mob shows up at the jail.
sentences.zh: 他因这场争吵而被捕并被带进监狱，随后在半夜，一群暴徒出现在监狱外。

sentences.en: They drag him out of his jail cell in his pajamas and they murder him in cold blood.
sentences.zh: 他们把他穿着睡衣从牢房里拖出来，冷血地杀害了。

sentences.en: After Thomas Moss is killed, Ida B.

sentences.zh: 已解锁？

sentences.en: Everyone knows you need to subscribe to the Times to access all of the reporting.
sentences.zh: 众所周知，你需要订阅《时报》才能阅读所有报道。

sentences.en: But what if you could explore the Times for a month, for free, without putting in a credit card?
sentences.zh: 但如果能免费试用《时报》一个月，且无需绑定信用卡，会怎么样？

sentences.zh: 首次下载《纽约时报》应用，即可享受第一个月的免费体验。

sentences.en: If you don't already subscribe to the New York Times, download the Times app today and get free access for 30 days.

sentences.en: The Free Speech, Memphis, Tennessee, May 21st, 1892.
sentences.zh: 《自由言论报》，田纳西州孟菲斯，1892年5月21日。

sentences.en: Eight Negroes lynched since last issue of the Free Speech.
sentences.zh: 自从《自由言论报》上一期发行以来，已有八名黑人遭到私刑杀害。

sentences.en: One at Little Rock, Arkansas.
sentences.zh: 一名在阿肯色州小石城。

sentences.en: She sets out on a reporting mission across the South, and she chronicles dozens and dozens of similar cases to find out what's really going on.
sentences.zh: 她开始在南方进行调查采访，记录了数十起类似案件，以弄清究竟发生了什么。

sentences.en: She conducts extensive interviews.
sentences.zh: 她进行了广泛的采访。

sentences.en: She pulls official records.
sentences.zh: 她调阅了官方档案。

sentences.en: She does data analysis.
sentences.zh: 她进行了数据分析。

sentences.en: August 31st at
sentences.zh: 8月31日于

sentences.en: Yarborough, Texas, and on September 19th at Houston, a colored man was found lynched.
sentences.zh: 德克萨斯州雅博勒，以及9月19日于休斯顿，发现了一名有色人种男子遭到私刑杀害。

sentences.en: But so little attention was paid to the matter that not only was no record made as to why these last two men were lynched, but even their names were not given.
sentences.zh: 但这件事受到的关注实在太少，不仅没有记录说明这两名男子为何被处以私刑，甚至连他们的名字都没有提及。

sentences.en: I mean, in many ways, Wells comes up with the blueprint for investigative journalism that we still use today.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，在许多方面，韦尔斯开创了我们至今仍在使用的调查新闻蓝图。

sentences.en: And she does it because, remember, she's a Black woman in the South who was born a slave.
sentences.zh: 她之所以能做到这一点，是因为别忘了，她是一个生为奴隶的南方黑人女性。

sentences.en: She doesn't have any inherent authority.
sentences.zh: 她没有任何固有的权威。

sentences.en: So she has to create it, and she does it with evidence.
sentences.zh: 所以她必须自己创造权威，而她是用证据做到的。

sentences.en: So this whole genre is kind of created out of necessity.
sentences.zh: 所以这种整个流派可以说是应运而生。

sentences.en: So because of her position, her status as a Black woman who probably didn't have the professional
sentences.zh: 因此，由于她的立场、她作为黑人女性的身份，她可能没有那种专业的人脉

sentences.en: networks, it sounds like that's what forces her to be so thorough, to be so enterprising, and so dogged.
sentences.zh: 网络，听起来正是这些迫使她如此彻底、如此具有进取心、如此坚韧不拔。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 完全正确。

sentences.en: To come up with these airtight arguments that white people who may not have otherwise listened to her can't deny.
sentences.zh: 从而提出这些无懈可击的论点，让那些本来可能不会听她说话的白人也无法反驳。

sentences.en: And what kinds of cases did she find?
sentences.zh: 她发现了什么样的案件？

sentences.en: Who was lynched?
sentences.zh: 谁遭到了私刑？

sentences.en: And what was the reason given for the lynching?
sentences.zh: 施以私刑的理由是什么？

sentences.en: Rape.
sentences.zh: 强奸。

sentences.en: Attempted rape.
sentences.zh: 企图强奸。

sentences.en: Alleged rape.
sentences.zh: 涉嫌强奸。

sentences.en: Suspicion of rape.
sentences.zh: 有强奸嫌疑。

sentences.en: In the vast majority of cases, she finds they begin with a Black man who's accused of raping a white woman.
sentences.zh: 在绝大多数案件中，她发现这些事件都始于一个被指控强奸白人女性的黑人男子。

sentences.en: And so that particular allegation, she really zeroes in on.
sentences.zh: 因此，对于这个特定的指控，她进行了深入研究。

sentences.en: She decides to question it.
sentences.zh: 她决定对此提出质疑。

sentences.en: And she does a systematic study in which she finds that there's very rarely any evidence of a sexual assault having taken place.
sentences.zh: 她进行了一项系统性研究，发现几乎没有任何证据表明发生过性侵犯。

sentences.en: And instead, in fact, she very often finds evidence of what was a consensual interracial relationship.
sentences.zh: 相反，事实上，她经常发现这是两情相悦的跨种族恋情证据。

sentences.en: And she publishes her findings in a series of editorials in the newspaper that she compiles under the title Southern Horrors.
sentences.zh: 她将自己的调查结果发表在报纸的一系列社论中，并以《南方恐怖》为题汇编成册。

sentences.en: And her findings are really upsetting to people, not just because of what she says, but because of how she says it.
sentences.zh: 她的发现确实让人感到不安，不仅因为她说了什么，还因为她表达的方式。

sentences.en: She writes, nobody in this section of the country believes the threadbare old lie that Negro men rape white women.
sentences.zh: 她写道，这个国家的这个地区没有人相信黑人男子强奸白人女性这种陈腐的谎言。

sentences.en: I mean, she really does not pull any punches at a time when it is not accepted for Black men and white women to be together.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，在当时黑人男性和白人女性在一起不被接受的年代，她真的是毫不留情。

sentences.en: So she's, through her reporting, showing that the rationale for what is already a kind of shockingly unjustified act is bogus.
sentences.zh: 因此，她通过自己的报道表明，这种本身就已经令人震惊且毫无道理的行为，其背后的理由是虚假的。

sentences.en: It's fiction.
sentences.zh: 纯属虚构。

sentences.en: Caitlin, why was this important to Wells?
sentences.zh: 凯特琳，为什么这对韦尔斯如此重要？

sentences.en: Why did she feel the need to document these lynchings in such fine detail?
sentences.zh: 为什么她觉得有必要如此详细地记录这些私刑？

sentences.en: She writes about how the people who are lynched are sort of forgotten.
sentences.zh: 她写到了那些遭受私刑的人是如何被某种程度地遗忘的。

sentences.en: They're very often nameless, faceless.
sentences.zh: 他们往往没有名字，没有面孔。

sentences.en: No one knows their stories.
sentences.zh: 没有人知道他们的故事。

sentences.en: And so that becomes really important to her.
sentences.zh: 因此，这变得对她非常重要。

sentences.en: She thinks it's important to remember that these were real people with full lives, with families.
sentences.zh: 她认为重要的是要记住，这些人是有血有肉、拥有完整人生和家庭的真实个体。

sentences.en: Thomas Moss had a two-year-old child and his wife was pregnant when he was killed.
sentences.zh: 托马斯·莫斯被害时，有一个两岁的孩子，他的妻子当时正怀着孕。

sentences.en: My eyes filled with tears as I thought of the list of unfortunates.
sentences.zh: 当我想到那一长串不幸的人时，我的双眼充满了泪水。

sentences.en: They had no requiem.
sentences.zh: 他们没有安魂曲。

sentences.en: And like many a brave Union soldier, their bodies lay in many an unknown and unhonored spot.
sentences.zh: 就像许多勇敢的联邦士兵一样，他们的尸体躺在许多无人知晓、无人颂扬的角落。

sentences.en: She writes that if she didn't tell these stories, her subjects would be forgotten by all, save the night wind, no memorial service to bemoan their sad and horrible fate.
sentences.zh: 她写道，如果她不讲这些故事，她的采访对象将被所有人遗忘，除了夜风，没有任何追悼会去哀悼他们悲惨而可怕的命运。

sentences.en: How did people react to this very uncomfortable line of reporting?
sentences.zh: 人们对这种极不舒服的报道路线作何反应？

sentences.en: Very aggressively, very violently.
sentences.zh: 非常具有攻击性，非常暴力。

sentences.en: Stories are written about her that call her a harlot and a courtesan in the press.
sentences.zh: 媒体上开始出现关于她的文章，称她为娼妓和交际花。

sentences.en: And she's seen as this sort of tactless aggressor, the likes of which people really have never seen before and they don't know what to do with.
sentences.zh: 她被视为这种不讲情面的攻击者，人们从未见过这样的人，也不知道该如何应对。

sentences.en: Her newspaper is ransacked and she's lucky that she wasn't there.
sentences.zh: 她的报社被洗劫一空，幸运的是她当时不在那里。

sentences.en: Many people think that she would have been killed.
sentences.zh: 许多人认为她本会被杀害。

sentences.en: Her life is threatened and she actually has to leave the South after these editorials are published.
sentences.zh: 她的生命受到了威胁，这些社论发表后，她实际上不得不离开南方。

sentences.en: And she never goes back because she's not safe anymore.
sentences.zh: 她再也没有回去，因为她不再安全了。

sentences.en: Then what happens to her?
sentences.zh: 那她后来怎么样了？

sentences.en: She moves to Chicago where she continues to work as an activiSt. She helps to found some really prominent civil rights organizations, including the NAACP.
sentences.zh: 她搬到了芝加哥，在那里继续从事维权活动。她帮助创立了一些非常著名的民权组织，包括全国有色人种协进会（NAACP）。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: But it doesn't laSt. She's soon edged out of the leadership of this organization and others by names you know, like Booker T.
sentences.zh: 但这并没有持续多久。她很快就被你所熟知的人物（如布克·T）以及其他人挤出了该组织及其他组织的领导层，

sentences.en: Washington, W.E.B.
sentences.zh: Washington, W.E.B.

sentences.en: Du Bois, people who were much more conservative in their tactics, who were much more willing to be diplomatic when it came to the way that they communicated their causes.
sentences.zh: 杜波依斯，这些人在策略上要保守得多，在表达诉求时更愿意采取外交手段。

sentences.en: And she just wasn't.
sentences.zh: 而她根本不是这样。

sentences.en: Diplomatic with the white community, I assume.
sentences.zh: 我猜她对白人社群并不讲究外交手段。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 完全正确。

sentences.en: So her popularity really ebbs pretty dramatically later in life.
sentences.zh: 所以在她晚年，她的知名度确实急剧下降。

sentences.en: She runs for the state senate in Illinois, but she loses pretty badly.
sentences.zh: 她在伊利诺伊州竞选州参议员，但输得很惨。

sentences.en: And then she dies when she's just 68 years old of kidney disease in 1931.
sentences.zh: 然后在1931年，她因肾病去世，年仅68岁。

sentences.en: And even though she's arguably the most famous African-American woman of her time, her death was barely noted by the public.
sentences.zh: 尽管她可以说是她那个时代最著名的非裔美国女性，但她的死几乎没有引起公众的注意。

sentences.en: She doesn't even get an obituary in the New York
sentences.zh: 她甚至没有在《纽约

sentences.en: Times.
sentences.zh: 时报》上获得一篇讣告。

sentences.en: It strikes me as painfully ironic that it was her life's mission to document this era and these injustices.
sentences.zh: 这让我感到一种痛苦的讽刺：她一生的使命就是记录这个时代和这些不公正现象。

sentences.en: But then she herself and her life didn't get documented.
sentences.zh: 但随后她自己和她的一生却没有被记录下来。

sentences.en: It is ironic.
sentences.zh: 这确实很讽刺。

sentences.en: And she's left out of a lot of Black history.
sentences.zh: 她被排除在了许多黑人历史之外。

sentences.en: So, you know, I think she came so far before her time, not just as an African-American, but as an African-American woman.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，我认为她远远超越了她所处的时代，不仅作为一名非裔美国人，而且作为一名非裔美国女性。

sentences.en: And for as much of an impact as she was able to make, she was one person.
sentences.zh: 尽管她能够产生巨大的影响，但她终究只是一个人。

sentences.en: So she knew how easy it was for this kind of thing to happen.
sentences.zh: 所以她深知这种事情发生得有多么容易。

sentences.en: And that's precisely why she focused so intensely on keeping records and proving the humanity of African-Americans, proving that Black people are worthy of the same treatment as
sentences.zh: 正因如此，她才如此专注地进行记录并证明非裔美国人的尊严，证明黑人值得享有与

sentences.en: whites.
sentences.zh: 白人相同的待遇。

sentences.en: And in fact, she writes,
sentences.zh: 事实上，她写道，

sentences.en: The Afro-American is not a bestial race.
sentences.zh: 非裔美国人绝不是一个野蛮的种族。

sentences.en: If this work can contribute in any way toward proving this and at the same time arouse the conscience of the American people to demand for justice to every
sentences.zh: 如果这项工作能在任何方面为证明这一点做出贡献，同时唤醒美国人民的良知，要求伸张正义、公正对待每一位

sentences.en: citizen and punishment for law by the lawless, I shall feel I have done my racist service.
sentences.zh: 公民，并依法惩治无法无天之徒，我将觉得我完成了我的种族使命。

sentences.en: Other considerations are of minor importance.
sentences.zh: 其他考量都是次要的。

sentences.en: The writings of Ida B.
sentences.zh: 艾达·B·

sentences.en: Wells were voiced by Michelle Duster, who for 10 years has been trying to dedicate a monument in Chicago in recognition of her great-grandmother, Ida B.

sentences.en: At the same time, President Trump joined Britain in accusing Russia of using a military-grade nerve

sentences.zh: 毒剂谋杀前俄罗斯间谍，这一攻击促使首相

sentences.en: Theresa May to expel 23 Russian diplomats earlier this week.
sentences.zh: 特雷莎·梅在本周早些时候驱逐了23名俄罗斯外交官。

sentences.zh: 这看起来确实是俄罗斯人在背后操纵。

sentences.en: Something that should never, ever happen.
sentences.zh: 这是绝对、绝对不应该发生的事情。

sentences.en: And we're taking it very seriously, as I think are many others.
sentences.zh: 我们正在非常严肃地对待此事，我想许多其他人也是如此。

sentences.zh: 还有……

sentences.en: Good evening, everyone.
sentences.zh: 大家晚上好。

sentences.zh: 我是拉里·库德洛。

sentences.en: You know, he's so good on taxes.

sentences.zh: 他在放松管制、基础设施建设方面表现太棒了。

sentences.en: I even like him on immigration.
sentences.zh: 我甚至很喜欢他在移民问题上的立场。

sentences.en: He's never been good on trade.
sentences.zh: 他在贸易问题上一向表现糟糕。

sentences.en: For decades, the Brooklyn Democratic Party operated as a tightly controlled machine.
sentences.zh: 几十年来，布鲁克林民主党一直作为一个受严密控制的机器运作。

sentences.en: Until this summer, when elections ushered in a bunch of self-described reformers.
sentences.zh: 直到今年夏天，选举迎进了一群自称改革派的人。

sentences.en: Ever since, the party has been in the grip of a bruising, chaotic, and sometimes thrilling fight.
sentences.zh: 从那以后，该党一直陷入一场残酷、混乱、有时甚至令人惊心动魄的争斗中。

sentences.en: In the latest episode of Metro, with me, Sarah Koenig, stories of people trying to maintain their influence and losing control along the way.
sentences.zh: 在最新一期的《都会》节目中，我将与萨拉·科尼格一起，讲述人们试图维持影响力却最终失控的故事。

sentences.en: Metro.
sentences.zh: 《都会》。
